name: Poland
sources: No per-nation sourcing note existed when this nation was first entered in init.rs; the table header recorded only "Transcribed-not-invented: approximate 1990 historical starting conditions". The figures were moved into this file unchanged, and their origin remains undocumented. What follows is what the 1990 record actually says, added so the gap is visible rather than inherited.

The Balcerowicz programme took effect on 1 January 1990 — the game opens on its first day. CPI inflation for the year came to 585.8% (GUS), and output fell 11.6%. The National Bank's refinancing rate was raised to 36% a month in January and cut through the year as prices came off.

inflation 0.55 is therefore NOT the 1990 print. On this directory's fraction-of-1 convention 585.8% is 5.858; 0.55 is that figure shifted one decimal place, the same shift Brazil and Yugoslavia carry and the same three nations whose percentage needed four digits. See brazil.json for why the true figure cannot simply be entered: inflation is hard-clamped into -0.05..=3.0 in economy.rs, and the real-rate demand channel is linear and unbounded, so 5.858 against any plausible policy rate drives GDP through zero. The loader refuses it since this commit.

The cost is the same shape as Brazil's and worth naming. interest_rate 0.3 against inflation 0.55 is a real rate of -25 points, the second-loosest opening position in the roster, which the demand channel reads as a large stimulus. Poland accordingly grows about 7% through 1990 on seed 1 — $66bn to $70.7bn — where the transition depression was an 11.6% contraction. The direction of Poland's first two years is wrong, and it is the real rate that makes it wrong, not the inflation figure on its own.

pop_growth_1990 = 0.5666%/yr. Compound annual growth of World Bank SP.POP.TOTL, series POL (Poland): 36,904,134 in 1984 to 37,961,529 in 1989 — the five years ending on the eve of the 1 January 1990 start date. See EconomyRecord::pop_growth_1990 in spheres-sim/src/data/mod.rs for why the window ends in 1989 and not with the single-year 1990 rate.

note: 1990 TECHNOLOGY: AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED. What this nation knew on 1 January 1990 is transcribed and sourced grant by grant, exactly like every other 1990 figure in this file, and is not read off tfp_trend - there was never a code path from the trend to the known set, and the zero that stood there was a claim about the world rather than an absence of one (BIBLE section 8 and iron rule 4, both amended 2026-08-30). THE PREDICATE IS SPLIT, and split by the technology's OWN EFFECT TYPE so that it is mechanically computable and never a per-nation judgement call. A node whose effects include MilitaryEfficiency, MilitaryStrength, DiffusionEmission or CostReduction is SOVEREIGNTY-SIDE: holding it means this nation could PRODUCE it, so operating an imported article does not qualify. Every other node is USE-SIDE: deployed and in operational use here is enough, whoever built it, because the effect such a node pays is a productivity, health or output effect and that effect is real in the country where the machine runs. Of the 48 technologies the tree lets anyone hold in 1990, 17 are sovereignty-side and 31 are use-side.

ALL 48 OF THE 1990-ELIGIBLE TECHNOLOGIES WERE RULED FOR THIS NATION, one at a time, against a standard published per technology rather than per country. 1 were held and are listed below with their citations; 47 were refused. The refused ids are named at the end of this note so that a reader can tell a cell that was examined and refused from a cell nobody looked at - those are different claims and the schema would otherwise flatten them into the same silence.

RULED AND REFUSED, ids only (the reasoning for each refusal is held with the board that wrote it, one standard per technology): core_cmos_submicron, core_packet_internetworking, core_single_mode_fiber, core_carbon_composites, core_combined_cycle_turbine, core_pcr, comp_microprocessor, comp_risc_superscalar, comp_relational_database, comm_digital_switching, comm_fibre_optic_backbone, comm_geostationary_comsat, comm_cellular_analogue, ener_seismic_3d_imaging, ener_horizontal_drilling, ener_gas_turbine_combined_cycle, ener_crystalline_silicon_module, matl_semiconductor_lithography, matl_composite_structures, matl_industrial_robotics, matl_lean_production, matl_single_crystal_superalloy, matl_rare_earth_magnet, matl_stereolithography, aero_precision_munitions, aero_pulse_doppler_radar, aero_stealth_shaping, aero_quiet_submarine, aero_recon_satellite, bio_recombinant_pharma, bio_oral_rehydration, bio_cross_sectional_imaging, bio_conjugate_vaccine, bio_monoclonal_antibody, bio_automated_sequencing, tran_container_intermodal, tran_post_panamax_ship, tran_electronic_freight_documents, tran_high_speed_rail, agri_drip_irrigation, agri_composite_membrane, agri_conservation_tillage, agri_integrated_pest_management, agri_protected_cultivation, agri_tissue_culture_propagation, agri_marine_aquaculture, agri_flue_gas_desulphurisation.
